item.title: Implement token-bucket rate limiter per SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py` (the module currently only has stubs). Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases; the tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics. Keep it dependency-free (standard library only) and commit your work."

Goal: replace the NotImplementedError stubs in ratelimit.py with working TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter classes exactly as SPEC.md defines them.

Constraints:
- Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the authority. Implement every rule: ValueError for capacity/refill_per_sec <= 0, for n <= 0 or n > capacity, and for max_keys < 1; new buckets start full; fractional tokens; tokens never exceed capacity; wait_time does not consume tokens and returns 0.0 when acquirable now; clock going backwards changes nothing until it passes the latest time already seen; KeyedLimiter LRU eviction where try_acquire and wait_time both count as use, evicted keys restart full; len() returns the number of tracked keys.
- Time is read only via the injected clock callable. No other dependency (standard library only; the module already imports time, keep it at most).
- Keep functions under 60 lines, flat control flow, at least two meaningful assertions or explicit validation at the boundary, no try/except that hides errors, no unnecessary comments.
- Add tests for the edge cases in SPEC.md (error cases, clock going backwards, eviction order including use via wait_time, evicted key returns full, fractional refill, cap at capacity, wait_time not consuming tokens) to test_ratelimit.py. Keep the existing tests passing.
- Run `python -m unittest` in the repository and make sure it passes before finishing.
- Commit the work to the current branch with a clear message. Do not push. Commit as the configured git user only; do not add generated-by or Claude attribution lines.
- Do not change SPEC.md.

evidence.caption: python -m unittest on the base commit: all tests error with NotImplementedError

pr.body: Approach: ratelimit.py replaces the stubs. TokenBucket refills from an injected clock and never moves its latest-seen time backwards. try_acquire is an exact tokens >= n check. wait_time returns 0.0 when acquirable now, otherwise deficit/rate plus a small padding (4 ulp of clock and token arithmetic) so that advancing the clock by it always succeeds. KeyedLimiter keeps an OrderedDict of buckets; try_acquire and wait_time both count as use; n is validated before any eviction. Files: ratelimit.py, test_ratelimit.py. Checks: python -m unittest, 18 tests OK. Probe: 50000 random cases per clock base (-1e8, 0, 1e6, 1e8, 1e9) gave 0 misses and 0 early admits. Assumptions: the padding makes wait_time exceed the exact time by about 1e-7 s at large clocks; otherwise the spec's exact semantics are kept. Standard library only.
pr.summary: Made the rate limiter work: TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter now implement SPEC.md. Now: validated params, start-full buckets, exact try_acquire, wait_time padded for clock rounding, LRU eviction of keys. Before: both classes raised NotImplementedError.
pr.title: Implement token-bucket rate limiter per SPEC

agt_01M88QSGZ0Q6T1B4481AKZHZ0Z:1.description: wait_time() is not reliable at realistic monotonic clock values. _has_tokens uses an absolute-scale rel_tol=1e-12 against n, but the clock's float rounding grows with its magnitude. Advancing the clock by wait_time() then leaves try_acquire() False. Reproduced: clock base 1e6, TokenBucket(7, 49.0), try_acquire(7), wait_time(7)=0.142857..., advance, try_acquire(7) is False. Base 1e8 failed 7 of 72

agt_01M88QSGZ0Q6T1B4481AKZHZ0Z:2.description: Test coverage gap: test_advancing_by_wait_time_always_succeeds only uses clock values starting at 0.0, so it cannot catch the large-clock failure above. Add a case with a large starting clock (e.g. 1e6 or 1e8). at test_ratelimit.py:104

agt_01M88QSGZ0Q6T1B4481AKZHZ0Z:3.description: _has_tokens also accepts available slightly below n (within 1e-12 relative), and the subsequent max(0.0, ...) clamp admits the request. This is a tiny over-admission that departs from the SPEC's 'remove nothing and return False' wording. Acceptable only if the tolerance is redesigned. at ratelimit.py:8

agt_01M88QVRD7DDKE5XMH9M9XGXKK:1.description: The new slack 4*ulp(clock)*refill_per_sec is in tokens and grows with rate. At high rate and large clock it admits whole tokens from an empty bucket, which breaks SPEC's rule that try_acquire succeeds only with at least n tokens. Probe: capacity 1, base 1e8, rate 1e8: try_acquire(1) on an empty bucket returns True; base 1e9, rate 1e7: True. This is the admission-slack concern in agt_01M88QSGZ0Q6T1

agt_01M88QVRD7DDKE5XMH9M9XGXKK:2.description: The slack uses math.ulp(max(1.0, self._last)). For a negative clock the ulp is taken at 1.0, which is far too small. Probe: base -1e8 gives 24111 of 50000 wait-then-acquire misses, while bases 0, 1e6, 1e8 and 1e9 give 0. The spec does not say the clock is non-negative, but time.monotonic is in practice. Fix is abs(self._last) in place of self._last. at ratelimit.py:42

risk.why: New standard-library module with no security, auth or concurrency surface; behaviour follows SPEC.md, verified by 18 tests and a randomized probe. Reviewer agt_01M88QYWYFHR49FBR4T9DJB9KQ set low after the exact-admission fix. Earlier reviews rated medium and found float-precision bugs, now fixed.
